biggest_catch: The friend must fund at least $250 into a share account within 60 days (or fund a loan within 90 days) - a join-only referral with no funding earns you nothing, and the promo window is fixed.
catches: Referrer: current SF Fire member 18+; register at sffirecu.org/refer and share your unique link.

Friend must: register via your link; join SF Fire CU by opening a share account (checking/savings/money market/certificate) or a loan product; fund $250+ into the share account within 60 days of membership or have the loan funded within 90 days.
Indirect loans and trust/estate accounts ineligible; referred member cannot have previously been an SF Fire member.
Reward: $50 Mastercard Virtual Reward per qualifying referral, up to $500 per calendar year.
Both accounts must be open and in good standing at reward issuance; reward not transferable; 2-3 weeks for virtual delivery (4-6 weeks for physical card if not subscribed to marketing emails).
Promo window: September 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026; can change without notice.
$600+ in prizes in a calendar year triggers an IRS Form 1099.

steps: Register at sffirecu.org/refer to access your referral portal.
Invite friends with your unique referral link via email or social media.
Friend registers via your link, joins SF Fire CU, and funds $250+ into a share account within 60 days (or funds a loan within 90 days).
You receive a $50 Mastercard Virtual Reward per qualifying referral, up to $500/year.
timing: Mastercard Virtual Reward delivered 2-3 weeks after all requirements completed.
when_cash_arrives: Mastercard Virtual Reward delivered 2-3 weeks after all requirements completed. Roughly a month from the trigger event to cash in hand.
maximize: Trigger the clock early: have your friend complete qualifying activity (direct deposit, debit transactions) in the first days of the window.
Route a real payroll direct deposit (not Zelle/P2P transfers, which most programs exclude) as early as possible - payroll timing is usually the gating step.
If any-amount direct deposit qualifies, a small recurring ACH can trigger it - check the program's 'qualifying deposit' definition first.
Structural reason it cannot be faster: the payout window itself is 3-4 weeks after qualification - there is no expedited track.
